# RV power station and solar panel combos

The right pick depends on whether you need to run a roof air conditioner. A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

## If you want to run the AC or boondock full-time

**ALLPOWERS R4000 (3,456 Wh, 3,600 W at 120 V, 6,000 W peak)** is the best value in these results.
- It has an RV outlet, LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,500+ cycles, and a 5-year warranty.
- It accepts up to 2,000 W of solar over three 650 W inputs (12-60 V). You need panels on all three inputs to reach that. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a install-and-leave unit.
- The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 took it to $1,319.12 in a cart test on 2026-10-23, and it expires 2026-11-15. It requires an order over $1,200. Codes generally don't stack, and the store's checkout has the final word.
- The return policy is 30 days for unused items, and sale items may not be returnable.
- [Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. The specs and codes come from that same page, not independent testing.

**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W, 8,000 W surge)** is the best all-rounder.
- It's expandable past 12 kWh, charges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet, and runs under 30 dBA at low load.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and is the most expensive option once you add batteries.
- Pricing and purchase links are on the [EmergencyEnergy comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). I don't have a verified current price. That article is written for Ontario, so ignore its Canadian electrical rules.

The same article also lists the Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024 Wh, 3,000 W) as a simpler pick for AC-focused weekends.

## Mid-size RV or van

**BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W)** has a built-in 30A RV port and accepts up to 1,200 W of solar. It weighs about 62 lb. It's the best fit if you plan to run a big rooftop or ground array ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Weekend trips

- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W)** accepts up to 1,000 W of solar across two inputs and expands to 5 kWh. It's the top overall pick in [SmartEnergyEdge's ranking](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W)** is the lightest at about 24 lb, but it has a 400 W solar cap. Two SolarSaga 200 W panels use all of it. Its ecosystem is the simplest, and Jackery has the most consistent support ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).

## Matching solar to the station

A power station's solar input limit caps what your panels can deliver. Extra panels past that limit are wasted ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)). Check the station's voltage range as well.

For small setups, [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) suggests a Renogy 200 W foldable solar suitcase. The results didn't include direct purchase links or current prices for specific panels. I'd rather not guess at those, so check the manufacturer's page for voltage and connector compatibility before buying.

## Caveats

- Several of these sources are affiliate sites. Their prices and some brand claims are dated, for example the June 2026 prices in the Outdoor Power Stations comparison and its 2-year Bluetti warranty, which another source puts at up to 5-6 years. Confirm current specs and warranty on the seller's page.
- Add up your loads first. A 150 W fridge running 10 hours is about 1,500 Wh. Tell me your appliances and whether you have a roof AC, and I can narrow this to one combo.
